hypotheses: SMER-3 at 10 uM for 24 h in A375 produces a histone-mark signature dominated by loss of H3K27me0K36me2, H3K27me1K36me2, H3K27me1K36me0, H3K27me1K36me1, and H3K27me0K36me3 with gain of H3K27me3K36me1, consistent with altered H3K27/H3K36 methylation crosstalk rather than a single-mark change.

Donors with high anchor similarity (Roscovitine, KU-55933, Etoposide, Resveratrol, momelotinib) are most likely to transfer a reproducible histone perturbation in A375 because their measured target-minus-A375 response profiles resemble the SMER-3 anchor signature.

If the transferred donor response is driven by H3K27me3K36me1 gain and H3K27me1K36me2 loss, the selected target feature should be one of these opposing marks to maximize the chance of a >0.5 log2 histone perturbation versus vehicle.
object.evidence_gap: No direct SMER-3 histone-mark response measurements or mechanism-specific donor pharmacology are provided; donor selection relies on anchor similarity and must be validated by retrieving donor response values before any transfer or causal interpretation.
